articles.title: TSMC reports strong 2nm yield ramp ahead of 2027 volume production
articles.summary: TSMC signalled that its N2 node is tracking ahead of prior yield curves, with risk production expanding across Fab 20 in Hsinchu. Executives said early customer engagement for the node has outpaced N3 at the same stage, pointing to a faster ramp into full volume manufacturing by 2027.

articles.title: Nvidia unveils next-gen Rubin architecture roadmap details
articles.summary: Nvidia outlined packaging and memory bandwidth targets for its post-Blackwell Rubin platform, aimed at 2027 data centre deployment. The architecture is expected to pair with next-generation HBM4 memory and lean further on advanced CoWoS packaging to sustain the compute density AI customers are demanding.

articles.title: ASML High-NA EUV tool shipments accelerate into second half
articles.summary: ASML confirmed additional High-NA EUV units shipped to logic customers, a key enabler for sub-2nm patterning. The company said tool utilisation at early adopter sites is improving faster than expected, easing some concerns about the technology's readiness for high-volume manufacturing.

articles.title: US Commerce Department updates export control list for advanced packaging tools
articles.summary: New guidance narrows which advanced packaging and deposition tools can be shipped to certain markets without a licence. Industry groups noted the update is more targeted than earlier rounds of restrictions, focusing specifically on equipment tied to sub-3nm-class manufacturing rather than broader categories of chipmaking tools.

articles.title: Samsung Foundry courts new customers with 2nm GAA process pitch
articles.summary: Samsung is positioning its gate-all-around 2nm node as a differentiator to win back foundry customers from TSMC. The company is reportedly offering more flexible design-kit support and earlier engineering access in an effort to attract fabless customers who shifted orders away during the 3nm transition.

articles.title: Intel Foundry secures external customer commitment for 18A capacity
articles.summary: Intel Foundry announced a multi-year capacity agreement, a milestone in its push to become a credible external foundry. The deal is seen as an important proof point for Intel's turnaround strategy, following years of scepticism from analysts about whether the company could compete for outside foundry customers at all.

articles.title: AMD expands chiplet strategy with new interposer packaging partner
articles.summary: AMD's next MI-series accelerators will use a new interposer supplier to diversify advanced packaging capacity. The move reduces AMD's reliance on a single packaging vendor at a time when CoWoS-class capacity remains one of the tightest bottlenecks across the AI accelerator supply chain.

articles.title: Synopsys and Cadence both report AI-driven EDA revenue growth
articles.summary: Both major EDA vendors cited AI-assisted verification and place-and-route tools as a growing share of licensing revenue. Executives from each company pointed to shorter verification cycles as the clearest customer-facing benefit, with some large SoC design teams reporting double-digit reductions in time-to-tapeout.

articles.title: SK Hynix HBM4 samples ship to key AI accelerator customers
articles.summary: SK Hynix began sampling next-generation HBM4 memory stacks, targeting qualification for 2027 AI accelerator platforms. The company said early bandwidth figures are meeting internal targets, though full qualification across multiple customers is expected to take several more quarters.

articles.title: Qualcomm expands automotive chip design wins with two new OEMs
articles.summary: Qualcomm's Snapdragon Digital Chassis platform picked up new automaker design wins for ADAS and infotainment. The wins extend Qualcomm's push beyond mobile into automotive silicon, an area the company has identified as a key long-term growth market as smartphone chip demand growth slows.

articles.title: Applied Materials sees deposition equipment demand tied to gate-all-around transition
articles.summary: Demand for atomic-layer deposition tools is rising as foundries transition from FinFET to gate-all-around transistors. Applied Materials said the shift requires meaningfully more deposition and etch steps per wafer than FinFET, which is lifting equipment spend per node even as overall wafer starts stay flat.

articles.title: SMIC reportedly making incremental gains on mature-node yields amid equipment constraints
articles.summary: Industry analysts note steady but constrained progress at SMIC's mature nodes given continued equipment export limits. Without access to newer deposition and lithography tools, the company is reportedly relying on process optimisation and yield engineering rather than equipment upgrades to improve output.

articles.title: Arm reports record licensing quarter on strength of compute subsystems
articles.summary: Arm's pre-built compute subsystem offering continues to gain traction with data centre and mobile customers alike. The subsystems bundle CPU cores with interconnect and memory controllers already tuned for specific workloads, cutting the design time customers would otherwise need to integrate those pieces themselves.

articles.title: Micron raises capex guidance on HBM and DDR5 demand
articles.summary: Micron increased its fiscal-year capital expenditure outlook, citing sustained AI-driven memory demand. The company said HBM output is essentially sold out through 2027, and it is prioritising conversion of existing DRAM capacity toward HBM production over adding new greenfield capacity in the near term.

articles.title: Analog Devices completes acquisition of niche RF component maker
articles.summary: The deal adds specialised RF front-end IP to ADI's portfolio, aimed at defence and telecom customers. Terms were not disclosed, though analysts estimate the acquired firm's annual revenue in the low hundreds of millions, with the deal expected to close by the end of the fiscal year.

articles.title: TSMC Arizona fab reaches volume production milestone for 4nm
articles.summary: TSMC's first US fab reached commercial volume production, part of a broader push to diversify manufacturing geography. The Arizona site is expected to supply a growing share of chips for US-based customers who have faced pressure to reduce reliance on Taiwan-based fabrication for critical components.

articles.title: Nvidia and TSMC deepen CoWoS advanced packaging capacity agreement
articles.summary: The expanded agreement addresses a persistent bottleneck in CoWoS packaging capacity for AI accelerators. Analysts have flagged CoWoS availability, rather than wafer supply itself, as the binding constraint on how many AI accelerators Nvidia can actually ship in any given quarter.

articles.title: EU Chips Act second phase funding allocated to pilot lines
articles.summary: The European Commission allocated additional funding to pilot production lines for next-generation chip packaging. The programme is intended to help European firms close the gap in advanced packaging capability, an area where the region has historically lagged behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the United States.

articles.title: Cadence launches new AI-assisted verification platform
articles.summary: The new platform aims to cut verification cycle times for large SoC designs using generative AI assistance. Cadence said early customers using the tool on production designs have seen meaningful reductions in bug-finding time during the pre-tapeout verification stage, though full-scale rollout is still limited to select partners.

articles.title: Texas Instruments expands 300mm analogue fab capacity in Texas
articles.summary: TI's new 300mm facility is aimed at expanding domestic analogue and power chip capacity over the next several years. The company has emphasised that larger wafer sizes lower its per-unit manufacturing cost for the mature-node analogue parts that make up the bulk of its product portfolio.
